items.d: a closeness or similarity; a feeling of having a lot in common
items.e: I felt an [affinity] with the writer.
Her singing is more [akin to] Rihanna than Adele.

items.d: a comparison that helps explain something
items.e: To use a sporting [analogy], middle age is like half-time.
The picture doesn't [correspond to] the truth.
Don't [equate] price with value.
Apologising would be [tantamount to] admitting failure.

items.d: could be exchanged / impossible to tell apart
items.e: Her house was [indistinguishable] from the others.

items.d: made up of different types / very different and separate
items.e: The [disparate] regions of Spain all have unique customs.
This house is [not dissimilar to] the one I grew up in.
They have widely [divergent] opinions.

items.d: easy to recognise / separate, not overlapping
items.e: The car has a [distinctive] colour.

items.d: become more varied / move apart / find a difference
items.e: Farmers have had to [diversify].
They live in [comparative] comfort.
[I must admit] I didn't enjoy the film.
Lend you £1,000? [You must be joking]!

items.d: said to someone who looks worried
items.e: Cheer up – [it might never happen]!
I was in the park when [who should I see but] my boss.

items.t: Accidents will happen · I should be so lucky!
items.d: accidents are inevitable; that's not likely
items.e: Don't worry about the wine – [accidents will happen].
They're [bound to] get married in the end.
She's [unquestionably] the best student.

items.t: in all probability · the chances are · every likelihood
items.e: [In all probability] we'll finish on time.
items.es: con toda probabilidad; lo más seguro es que; todas las probabilidades

items.e: She'll be here by five, [for sure].

items.d: necessary; required by rules / you can choose
items.e: Wearing a helmet is [obligatory] here.
We [have an obligation to] protect the school's name.
I'm [determined] to help.
She [has aspirations to] become Prime Minister.
The owner [acceded] to the workers' demands.
The minister [acquiesced] in the plan.

items.d: agree to a plan or proposal
items.e: Shareholders [assented] to the takeover.

items.d: give official permission / give official approval
items.e: The cabinet has [endorsed] the proposal.

items.d: accept behaviour most think is wrong
items.e: We cannot [condone] violence.
No government would [countenance] abolishing taxes.
The committee was [given carte blanche] to fix the problem.

items.t: give the go-ahead / the green light
items.e: The city has [given the go-ahead] for the car park.
Three students were [barred] from the library.

items.d: use full power to limit something
items.e: The government is [clamping down on] tax evasion.
The President [vetoed] the plan.
She went to the party [regardless].
items.es: a pesar de todo; independientemente de

items.t: be fed up with / sick of
items.d: be tired of and annoyed by
items.e: I'm [fed up with] your moaning.
[I've had enough of] your stupid comments.

items.t: This is just not on! · Enough is enough!
items.e: You promised to be here at two – [this is just not on]!
You never help at home. [It just won't do]!

items.t: I wish to complain about · This is most unsatisfactory
items.e: [I wish to complain about] the delay.
items.es: quiero presentar una queja; esto es del todo insatisfactorio

items.e: I [take great exception to] your comments.
I [object to] being made to wait.

items.d: not tolerable / should make you feel guilty
items.e: Leaving the children in the rain was [shameful].
He [remonstrated] with the referee.
She always [finds fault with] my work.
Stop [whingeing] and get on with it!
He offered his most [heartfelt] apology.
It was a rather [lame] excuse.

items.t: a phoney explanation · a cast-iron alibi
items.d: a false explanation; a very firm alibi
items.e: She had a [cast-iron] alibi.
items.es: una explicación falsa; una coartada a prueba de bombas

items.e: He came on the [flimsy pretext] of borrowing a book.

items.d: feel no guilt; say you're sorry
items.e: He [showed no remorse] whatsoever.
His companions were [acquitted] of the crime.

items.t: a posthumous pardon · exonerate · a reprieve
items.d: forgiveness after death; declare free of blame; official stop to punishment
items.e: The inquiry [exonerated] the minister.

items.d: stop being angry and forget what happened
items.e: It's hard for victims to [forgive and forget].

items.d: written agreement between countries; agreement to stop war; official agreement
items.e: The two nations signed a peace [treaty].

items.t: call a truce · agree to a ceasefire
items.e: The two politicians [called a truce].
items.es: declarar una tregua; acordar un alto el fuego

items.t: pay sb compliments · fish for compliments
items.d: say nice things; try to get praise
items.e: He was really only [fishing for compliments].
[Take it as a compliment] that he fell asleep!

items.d: praise that is also negative (malicious / innocent)
items.e: 'Good for your age' – that's a [back-handed] compliment.
He [complimented] me on my guitar playing.

items.t: praiseworthy · highly praised · praised to the skies
items.e: Her book was [praised to the skies].
items.es: loable; muy elogiado; puesto por las nubes

items.t: sing sb's praises · heap praise on
items.e: Everyone is [singing her praises].
items.es: cantar las alabanzas; colmar de elogios

items.d: praise so weakly that it seems critical
items.e: 'It was ... fine.' – that's [damning with faint praise].

items.t: pay tribute to · extol the virtues of
items.e: I [paid tribute to] his kindness.
items.es: rendir homenaje a; ensalzar las virtudes de

items.d: be admired for a recent success
items.e: She's now [the toast of] Hollywood.

items.t: a pat on the back · earn plaudits
items.e: The exhibition [earned plaudits] from reviewers.
items.es: una palmadita en la espalda; cosechar elogios

items.e: It's a [laudable] initiative.

items.t: suck up to · lick sb's boots · crawl
items.d: praise someone for your own benefit (informal)
items.e: He's always [sucking up to] the boss.

items.d: insincerely polite; too eager to please
items.e: The waiter was rather [obsequious].

items.t: Flattery will get you nowhere! · flatter (a figure)
items.d: insincere praise won't work; make look better
items.e: That dress really [flatters] her.
Politicians always [promise the earth].
items.es: prometer el oro y el moro

items.t: promise to be · show promise · promising
items.d: be expected to be; show talent
items.e: She [shows great promise] as a violinist.

items.d: make someone formally promise to tell the truth
items.e: Witnesses are [put under oath].

items.t: I could have sworn · I couldn't swear to it
items.d: I was certain / I'm not totally sure
items.e: [I could have sworn] I left my purse here.
items.es: juraría que; no lo puedo asegurar

items.e: My mother [swears by] these vitamin pills.

items.d: (v, n) promise (money, support) / make a determined promise
items.e: He [vowed] to find his father's killer.

items.t: make/keep/break a resolution · turn over a new leaf
items.d: promise to change; start behaving better
items.e: This year I'm going to [turn over a new leaf].
He [went back on his word].

items.d: money risked; at risk; a bet (formal)
items.e: Many lives will be [at stake].

items.t: your best bet · Don't bet on it! · You bet!
items.e: [Your best bet] is to look for a part-time job.
items.es: lo mejor que puedes hacer; yo no apostaría; ¡ya lo creo!

items.t: have a flutter · put money on · hedge your bets
items.d: make a small bet; be sure about; protect yourself against a wrong choice
items.e: Invest in several companies to [hedge your bets].
items.es: apostar un poco; apostar por; cubrirse las espaldas

items.t: out of touch · lose touch with
items.d: not up to date; stop being in contact
items.e: I've [lost touch with] him.

items.t: what became of · hear anything of
items.d: what happened to; receive news about
items.e: I wonder [what became of] our maths teacher.
items.es: qué fue de; saber algo de

items.d: if I remember correctly; think about the past
items.e: His name, [if I recall], was Mr Sanderson.

items.t: that takes me back · it's all coming back to me
items.d: that makes me remember; I'm starting to remember
items.e: [That takes me back] to the day my phone rang in class.
items.es: eso me trae recuerdos; ya me acuerdo

items.t: a vague memory · stand out in my mind
items.d: an unclear memory; be remembered most
items.e: What [stands out in my mind] is the freedom we had.
items.es: un vago recuerdo; lo que más recuerdo

items.d: talk about pleasant memories; pleasure and sadness about the past
items.e: We spent the evening [reminiscing] about school.
We look at the past [through rose-tinted spectacles].
The photo [reminded] me of my schooldays.

items.d: sudden sharp feelings of guilt; embarrassment and guilt
items.e: I felt [pangs of guilt].

items.d: regret very much; feel sad about (literary)
items.e: I [rue the day] we ever met.
Her complaints [tally with] other comments.

items.t: in full accord with · coincide with
items.d: completely agreeing with; be the same as
items.e: Your views [coincide with] mine.
items.es: totalmente de acuerdo con; coincidir con

items.t: conform to · approve of · meet with sb's approval
items.d: fit in with; think is good; be liked
items.e: The plan [met with] her approval.
items.es: ajustarse a; aprobar; contar con la aprobación

items.t: agree to differ · reach a consensus
items.d: accept you disagree; agree as a group
items.e: We couldn't agree, so we [agreed to differ].
items.es: aceptar que no estamos de acuerdo; llegar a un consenso

items.t: dissent · discord · a rift · a split · division
items.d: kinds of disagreement in a group
items.e: There's a growing [rift] in the party.
The airport plans are bound to [cause controversy].

items.d: agree by each giving something up
items.e: The two sides have [reached a compromise].
items.es: llegar a un acuerdo; transigir en

items.t: make concessions to · reach a settlement
items.d: accept some demands; reach an agreement
items.e: The government [made concessions to] the protesters.
items.es: hacer concesiones a; llegar a un acuerdo

items.e: We should [exercise some discretion].
